answer_1.quote: Our system, the Intent-Guided Assistant (IGA), combines controllable text generation with text infilling ; more specifically, we adapt the tag-based control of to include a set of rhetorical directives that our model learns to infill with relevant and fluent text.
answer_1.outputs: Generated text infills satisfying specified rhetorical directives (e.g., descriptive additions, idioms, paraphrases) based on user tags and context.

answer_2.quote: We compare IGA with ILM on automatic metrics such as ROUGE ) and self-BLEU ) following Rashkin et al. (2020), computing both scores against reference completions

answer_4.quote: three Mechanical Turkers are shown the gold completion as well as the generated text and asked to choose which is more fluent, coherent, and adequate at fulfilling the author intent, using a five-point scale to measure fine-grained preference.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators used a five-point scale to compare generated outputs with gold completions based on fluency, coherence, and adequacy.
